<details>
I evaluated only the code that runs when the PKGBUILD is sourced by `makepkg --printsrcinfo`: the top-level/global scope. Everything there is ordinary metadata and variable assignment — `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `depends`, `source`, `sha256sums`, and helper strings (`_beta`, `_commit`, `_tag`, `_base`).

Critically, there is no top-level command substitution (`$(...)` or backticks), no `eval`, and no `curl`/`wget`/`base64`/`chmod` executed at source time. The `_tag="v${pkgver}-beat6"` and `_base="${url}/releases/download/${_tag}"` lines use plain parameter expansion (`${...}`), not command substitution, so nothing is downloaded or executed during parsing. (The `beat6` string is a benign typo of `beta6` and, being just a URL fragment, has no execution effect here.) The `_archmap()` helper and `prepare()`/`build()`/`package()` bodies contain commands like `bsdtar`, `patch`, `cmake`, `install`, `patchelf`, and `find`, but those functions are only *defined* at source time and do not run during this step, so they are out of scope for this gate.

Nothing in the sourced scope downloads and runs a payload or exfiltrates data, so parsing this PKGBUILD is safe.
</details>
<evidence>
